items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'Waiting for the Rain', and answer.

"The astrologers had promised rain by the full moon. The full moon came and went, and the sky stayed as hard and blue as a cooking pot. But old Ponni sat by her door watching the line of ants climbing her wall with their eggs. 'Three days,' she said. 'Perhaps four. The ants always know.'"

Answer the following:
(i) What had the astrologers promised?
(ii) "As hard and blue as a cooking pot" is a …  (a) personification  (b) pun  (c) simile  (d) metaphor
(iii) On what is Ponni's prediction based?  (a) A radio report  (b) A dream  (c) Observation of nature (the ants' behaviour), not astrology  (d) A horoscope
(iv) What does this passage suggest about traditional knowledge?
items.answer: (i) Rain by the full moon. (ii) (c) simile (iii) (c) Observation of nature (the ants' behaviour), not astrology (iv) That careful observation of nature can be more reliable than superstition or astrology.
items.markingKey: (i) Rain by the full moon. (ii) (c) simile (iii) (c) Observation of nature (the ants' behaviour), not astrology (iv) That careful observation of nature can be more reliable than superstition or astrology. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
